author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Set internal resolution for phones, tablets, handhelds, and TVs
summary: Choose an internal resolution from screen density and sustained GPU headroom, test it with a fixed scene, and avoid wasting heat on pixels the display or game cannot reveal.
heroAlt: PCSX2 performance overlay showing a hardware-rendered frame and timing counters

blocks.text: Upscaling is a GPU budget, not a quality preset

The PS2 renders many games far below a modern display's panel resolution. Internal resolution increases the emulator's render target before Android scales the final frame. It can sharpen 3D edges, but it does not create detail in prerendered video or low-resolution textures, and each step increases bandwidth, shader work and heat. Screen size alone therefore cannot select the right value.
Begin at native for diagnosis, then increase one step at a time. Never compensate for a slow CPU-bound game by lowering resolution indefinitely; confirm whether GPU time actually changes.

Use the correct hardware renderer and a demanding scene with moving effects, not a static menu. Disable battery saver, start from a cool device and use the same brightness. On a TV, verify that Android is outputting the intended refresh rate; on a handheld, account for the panel's physical resolution rather than the resolution advertised by an external dock.

items: A verified game and repeatable two-minute scene.
Native resolution, Safe profile and stable renderer.
Performance overlay or consistent frame-rate observation.
Cool device and fixed display brightness.
Known target display resolution and refresh rate.
1. At native resolution, confirm the title reaches full emulation speed and record GPU time, temperature trend and visible artifacts.
2. Raise one resolution step and replay the same scene. Stop increasing when GPU time rises sharply, frame pacing worsens or the next step adds no visible detail.
3. For a phone, favor sustained stability over tiny edge improvements; for a larger tablet, test one additional step only if thermal headroom remains.
4. For handhelds, match the built-in panel first and create a separate TV profile when docked output needs more pixels.
5. Cold-start twice at the chosen value and save it per game if another title requires a different ceiling.

blocks.text: The chosen level should remain full speed after at least fifteen minutes, not just during a cool launch. Inspect thin lines, post-processing, bloom and UI elements for upscaling-specific seams. A higher number is not a pass when it introduces ghost lines or pushes the device into a lower sustained clock.

items: Full emulation speed persists after the device warms.
Frame pacing is no worse than the next lower setting.
No new seams, offsets or broken post-processing appear.
The visual improvement is visible at normal viewing distance.
External-display and handheld profiles do not overwrite each other unexpectedly.

blocks.text: When a title starts stuttering later in a session, return one step lower and retest from a cool start. If graphics broke only after upscaling, restore native before touching blending or manual GS fixes. Reset the per-game resolution override if the global setting was already appropriate.

items: Lower internal resolution one step.
Restore native to confirm an upscaling-only glitch.
Remove a stale per-game override after changing displays.
Clear only the experiment notes—not saves or caches unrelated to resolution.
Sharp opening scene, slow later session: thermal headroom was overestimated.
No visual gain: textures or video, not geometry, limit detail.
CPU-heavy title unchanged by resolution: graphics load is not the bottleneck.
TV judder at full speed: output refresh mismatch, not necessarily insufficient GPU power.

blocks.text: A good resolution profile is deliberately conservative. The spare GPU budget absorbs shader-heavy scenes, background Android activity and warmer ambient temperatures. Use the display as the destination and sustained timing as the judge, then spend remaining headroom on accuracy settings that fix real game behaviour.
